items.stem: Appraising whether a manager's outperformance reflects skill rather than luck typically requires:

options.text: A sufficiently long record and statistical significance of excess return
options.rationale: Correct: distinguishing skill from luck needs an adequate sample and significance testing of alpha.

options.text: A single quarter of strong returns
options.rationale: One quarter is far too short to infer skill.

options.text: The manager's own confidence in their process
options.rationale: Self-assessment is not evidence of statistical skill.

options.text: The size of the manager's marketing budget
options.rationale: Marketing spend is irrelevant to investment skill.

items.explanation: Correct: distinguishing skill from luck needs an adequate sample and significance testing of alpha.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: In manager due diligence, 'style drift' refers to:

options.text: A manager departing from the stated investment mandate or style over time
options.rationale: Correct: style drift is movement away from the declared mandate, a key monitoring concern.

options.text: A fall in the risk-free rate
options.rationale: Interest-rate moves are not style drift.

options.text: A change in the fund's custodian bank
options.rationale: Changing custodian is an operational, not style, matter.

options.text: An increase in the benchmark's dividend yield
options.rationale: Benchmark yield changes are not style drift.

items.explanation: Correct: style drift is movement away from the declared mandate, a key monitoring concern.

items.stem: Select TWO items that should form part of ongoing monitoring of an external manager.

options.text: Tracking performance against the agreed benchmark and mandate
options.rationale: Correct: comparing results to the mandate and benchmark is core monitoring.

options.text: Reviewing changes in key investment personnel
options.rationale: Correct: personnel turnover is a key monitoring signal.
Ongoing monitoring is required; 'hire and forget' is poor practice.
